purpose: When each 2004-05 end-of-season award was announced, who voted and how ballots were scored, researched October 2026. Dates and rules only: no real 2005 winner or vote is recorded or used.

status_values.derived: inferred from cited sources, reasoning given
status_values.design_choice: not verifiable for 2004-05; the simulation's documented choice

ballot_due.note: After the last regular-season games (2005-04-20) and before the first media award (2005-04-28); no source states the deadline.

awards.name: Most Improved Player
awards.note: Announced Thursday, April 28, 2005 (AP wire brief dated April 28; 5-3-1 scoring stated). Electorate: the first-place votes on the Basketball-Reference tally sum to 123 and its maximum is 615 (123 x 5); no release stating the panel size was read.

awards.name: Defensive Player of the Year
awards.note: Announced Monday, May 2, 2005 at an afternoon news conference (AP wire brief of May 3). Electorate: Basketball-Reference first-place votes sum to 125 and its maximum is 625 (125 x 5). Scoring 5-3-1 as for the other media awards (derived).

awards.name: Sixth Man of the Year
awards.note: Announced Tuesday, May 3, 2005; 'of 125 first-place votes ... from a panel of sportswriters and broadcasters' (AP via CBC). Basketball-Reference maximum 625 (125 x 5).

awards.name: Rookie of the Year
awards.note: NBA release May 4, 2005: '126 possible first-place votes'; five, three and one points.

awards.name: All-Rookie Teams
awards.voters: head coaches, not for their own players
awards.note: SportsTicker via ESPN, May 5, 2005: selected Thursday 'in voting by 30 coaches. Coaches were not permitted to vote for players on their own team.' A unanimous player therefore receives 58 points (29 x 2), the Basketball-Reference maximum. Scoring 2-1 as in 2003-04 (derived).

awards.name: Most Valuable Player
awards.note: NBA release May 8, 2005: 'A panel of 127 sportswriters and broadcasters'; 10, 7, 5, 3 and 1 points.

awards.name: Coach of the Year
awards.note: NBA release dated May 10, 2005 (published 9:37 p.m. ET): panel of sportswriters and broadcasters, five, three and one points. Electorate: Basketball-Reference first-place votes sum to 126 and its maximum is 630 (126 x 5).

awards.name: All-Defensive Teams
awards.voters: head coaches, not for their own players
awards.note: NBA club release published May 12, 2005: 'a voting panel that consisted of the NBA's 30 head coaches, who were asked to select NBA All-Defensive First and Second Teams by position'. Two points for a first-team vote, one for a second-team vote (sourced in the published tally). Own-player exclusion as in 2003-04 (derived).

awards.name: All-NBA Teams
awards.note: NBA release May 18, 2005: 'The 124-member voting panel ... voted for All-NBA First, Second and Third Teams by position with points awarded on a 5-3-1 basis.'

awards.name: Finals MVP
awards.note: Announced on court the night the Finals are clinched (sourced). Each panelist names one player (sourced). Ten ballots were counted in 2005 (bballhistorydatabase; contemporaneous Argentine coverage describes one of them as an online fan ballot), so the electorate is 10 (derived); treating all ten as media voters is the design choice. An even panel can split: a tie at the top is an engine decision draw (no published tie rule; the award has never been shared). A player on the losing club may win (Jerry West, 1969).
